answer: It is valid for a period of one year.

question: How far in advance must a container depot operator lodge a renewal request before the current licence ends?
answer: not less than thirty days prior to the date of expiration of the licence previously issued.
evidence: (1) A licence issued under section 3 may be renewed upon an application being submitted to the Director- General for that purpose in the Form as may be prescribed accompanied by the prescribed renewal fee, not less than thirty days prior to the date of expiration of the licence previously issued. (2) The Director-General shall renew a licence on receipt of an application under subsection (1), where- (a) the licensee has not violated or done anything in contravention of the terms and conditions of the licence issued; (b) the licensee has not contravened any provisions of this Act or any regulations made thereunder; or (c) the continuation of the container depot operation concerned will not have any adverse impact on the public. (3) The provisions of section 3 of this Act shall apply in respect of a licence issued on renewal under this section.

question: Under the proposed 20th Amendment to the Constitution, how many days before being placed on Parliament's Order Paper must a bill be published in the Gazette?
answer: Every Bill shall be published in the Gazette at least seven days before it is placed on the Order Paper of Parliament.
evidence: Article 78 of the Constitution is hereby amended as follows- (1) by the repeal of paragraph (1) thereof, and the substitution therefor of the following paragraph- “(1) Every Bill shall be published in the Gazette at least seven days before it is placed on the Order Paper of Parliament.”; and (2) by the insertion, immediately after paragraph (2) of that Article, of the following paragraph- “(3) Any amendment proposed to a Bill in Parliament shall not deviate from the merits and principles of such Bill.”.

question: Under the amended Telecommunication Levy law, how often is the levy calculated on the value of telecom services received?
answer: It is levied on the value of the supply of telecommunication services provided by any operator or provider, in respect of each month.
evidence: Section 2 of the Telecommunication Levy Act, No. 21 of 2011(hereinafter referred to as the “principal enactment”) is hereby repealed and the following section is substituted therefor:- 2. There shall be charged and levied from every person receiving any telecommunication service, a levy called Telecommunication Levy (hereinafter referred to as the “levy”), at such rate as specified in the Schedule hereto, on the value of the supply of telecommunication services provided by any operator or provider, on the receipt of such telecommunication services in respect of each month: Provided that no organization or individual to whom the provisions of the Diplomatic Privileges Act, No. 9 of 1996 applies shall be required to pay the levy referred to above.”.

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer: Notice can be sent in writing, by personal communication, by fax, or by any other electronic method that clearly identifies the bill and states that it has been dishonoured due to non‑acceptance or non‑payment.
evidence: Section 49 of the principal enactment is hereby amended by the repeal of subsection (5) of that section and the substitution therefor, of the following subsection: - “(5) The notice may be given in writing or by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means which sufficiently identify the bill, and intimate that the bill has been dishonoured by non-acceptance or non- payment.”.

question: Under the amended Factories Ordinance, how is a "young person" defined?
answer: It refers to an individual who has reached sixteen years of age but is still younger than eighteen.
evidence: Section 127 of the principal enactment is hereby amended in subsection (1) thereof by the repeal of the definition of the expression “young person”, and the substitution therefor, of the following definition:- “ “young person” means a person who has attained the age of sixteen years but is under the age of eighteen years;”.

question: Under the Counter Terrorism Bill, what conditions allow a police officer or someone acting on his authority to use force to stop a vehicle, boat, train or plane, and when may lethal force be employed?
answer: Where the person in charge of any vehicle, vessel, train or aircraft disobeys any order given by a police officer or any other person acting on his demand for halting any such vehicle, vessel, train or aircraft for the purposes of this Act, such police officer or the person may use such force as may be necessary to halt such vehicle. Provided however, any such force may be used only where all other means of halting the vehicle, vessel, train or aircraft have proved ineffective: Provided further, any such officer shall not use lethal force except in the exercise of private defence within the meaning of the Penal Code.
evidence: Where the person in charge of any vehicle, vessel, train or aircraft disobeys any order given by a police officer or any other person acting on his demand for halting any such vehicle, vessel, train or aircraft for the purposes of this Act, such police officer or the person may use such force as may be necessary to halt such vehicle: Provided however, any such force may be used only where all other means of halting the vehicle, vessel, train or aircraft have proved ineffective: Provided further, any such officer shall not use lethal force except in the exercise of private defence within the meaning of the Penal Code.

question: Under the proposed Rishad Bathiudeen Foundation law, what powers does the corporation have to carry out its purposes?
answer: It may acquire and hold any movable or immovable property, open, run or close bank accounts, borrow money with or without security, receive grants, donations or other assistance, invest its funds, erect buildings on its land, and hire, employ or dismiss officers and staff needed to achieve its objectives.
evidence: Subject to the provision of this Act and any other written law, the Corporation shall have the power to do, perform and execute, all such acts, matters and things what so ever as are necessary or desirable for the promotion, or furtherance of the objects of the Corporation or any one of them, including the power to acquire and hold property movable or immovable, to open, operate and close bank accounts, to borrow or raise money with or without security, to receive or collect grants or donation or any other assistance from persons or organizations in Sri Lanka or abroad, to invest its funds, to erect any building or structures on any land held by the Corporation and to engage, employ and dismiss officers and servants required for the carrying out of the objects of the Corporation.

question: Under the proposed Bureau of Rehabilitation law, what punishment does a staff member face if they assault, mistreat, or deliberately neglect a person undergoing rehabilitation?
answer: Any person employed in a Centre for Rehabilitation who without reasonable cause strikes, wounds, ill treats or willfully neglects any person under rehabilitation commits an offence under this Act and shall be liable on conviction after summary trial by a Magistrate to a fine not exceeding two hundred thousand rupees or imprisonment of either description for a period not exceeding eighteen months or to both such fine and imprisonment.
evidence: Any person employed in a Centre for Rehabilitation who without reasonable cause strikes, wounds, ill treats or willfully neglects any person under rehabilitation commits an offence under this Act and shall be liable on conviction after summary trial by a Magistrate to a fine not exceeding two hundred thousand rupees or imprisonment of either description for a period not exceeding eighteen months or to both such fine and imprisonment.

question: What penalty does the proposed Divineguma Development Act impose on anyone who violates any of its provisions or any rule made under it?
answer: The violator is guilty of an offence and, upon conviction after a summary trial by a magistrate, may be fined up to 2,500 rupees or sentenced to imprisonment for no more than two years.
evidence: Any person who acts in contravention of any of the provisions of the Act or any regulation or rule made thereunder, shall be guilty of an offence under this Act and shall on conviction after summary trial by a Magistrate be liable to a fine not exceeding two thousand five hundred rupees or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years.

question: Under the Personal Data Protection Bill, what considerations will the Data Protection Authority use when deciding the size of an administrative penalty for a data‑processing breach?

question: Under the proposed Hesha Friendship Foundation incorporation law, what power will the foundation have to create and modify its own internal rules, and who must follow them?
answer: The foundation may, at a general meeting where at least two‑thirds of members present agree, adopt rules on matters such as membership categories, election and removal of officers, committee duties, officer conduct, meeting procedures, property and finance management, and overall affairs, provided they do not conflict with this Act or other statutes; those rules can be changed or repealed in the same manner, and every member must abide by them.

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s Intellectual Property Act, what new category of subject will receive protection and how is it defined?
answer: Section 160 is amended to replace the words ‘protecting inventions, industrial designs, marks, trade names’ with ‘protecting inventions, industrial designs, marks, trade names, geographical indications’, and subparagraph (iv) is changed to read ‘the geographical indication of any goods including production process of products or goods or services’.
evidence: Section 160 of the principal enactment is hereby amended as follows:- (1) in paragraph ( b) of subsection (1), by the substitution for the words “protecting inventions, industrial designs, marks, trade names,” of the words “protecting inventions, industrial designs, marks, trade names, geographical indications,”; (2) by the repeal of subparagraph (iv) of paragraph ( b) of subsection (4) and the substitution therefor of the following:- “(iv) the geographical indication of any goods including production process of products or goods or services;”.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Sri Lanka Land Development Corporation Act, how does the makeup of the body listed in Section 6 change regarding the officials included?
answer: Section 6 is amended by removing sub‑paragraphs (ii) and (iii) of paragraph (a) of subsection (1) and replacing them with: (ii) an Additional Secretary of the Ministry of the Minister; and (iii) the Director‑General of the National Physical Planning appointed under section 5 of the Town and Country Planning Ordinance (Chapter 269).
evidence: Section 6 of the principal enactment is hereby amended by the repeal of subparagraphs (ii) and (iii) of paragraph (a) of subsection (1), and the substitution therefor, of the following: - “(ii) an Additional Secretary of the Ministry of the Minister; and (iii) the Director-General of the National Physical Planning appointed under section 5 of the Town and Country Planning Ordinance (Chapter 269); and”. 10 Sri Lanka Land Development Corporation (Amendment)

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer: The amendment substitutes the phrase that includes freight forwarders, non‑vessel operating common carriers and container operators with wording that only refers to freight forwarders and non‑vessel operating common carriers, thereby removing any reference to container operators.
evidence: The long title to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non-Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, No.10 of 1972, (hereinafter referred to as the “principal enactment”) is hereby amended by the substitution for the words “F REIGHT FORWARDERS, NON-VESSEL OPERATING COMMON CARRIERS, AND CONTAINER OPERATORS”, of the words “FREIGHT FORWARDERS AND NON-VESSEL OPERATING COMMON CARRIERS”. Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non-Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators (Amendment)

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, what modification is being made to the existing law?
answer: The amendment updates the sections listed in Column I of the Schedule by replacing the wording shown in Column II with the new wording shown in Column III.
evidence: The Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, No. 25 of 2005 (hereinafter referred to as the “principal enactment”) is hereby amended in the sections specified in Column I of the Schedule to this Act, by the substitution for the words specified in the corresponding entry in Column II of that Schedule, of the words specified in the corresponding entry in Column III of that Schedule.

question: What legislation establishes a charitable foundation for relief services in memory of Arundika Fernando and Godfrey Fernando?
answer: The bill incorporates the Arundika Fernando Relief Services and Godfrey Fernando Memorial Foundation as a legal entity.

question: Which recent law establishes a new authority to manage and oversee land administration in Sri Lanka as mandated by the Constitution?

question: What amendment was proposed in 2022 to change Sri Lanka's law governing how parliamentary voting is conducted?
answer: The bill seeks to amend the Parliamentary Elections Act of 1981, updating the rules and procedures for conducting parliamentary elections.

question: Which 2019 bill updated the 2007 law that regulates corporate entities in Sri Lanka?

question: What were the 2019 amendments to Sri Lanka's law governing the entry and exit of foreign visitors and Sri Lankan citizens?
answer: The bill updates the Immigrants and Emigrants Act to revise rules on visas, work permits, and the departure of Sri Lankan nationals and foreign nationals.
evidence: to amend the Immigrants and Emigrants Act (Chapter 351)

question: Which 2017 legislation introduced an income tax for assessment years beginning on April 1, 2017?
answer: The bill imposes income tax on individuals and entities for any year of assessment starting on or after 1 April 2017.
evidence: to provide for the imposition of Income Tax for any year of assessment commencing on or after April 1, 2017.
